blocking_findings.basis: source comparison; independently confirmed by /root/query_migration; actual old/new public-ABI reproduction is delegated and not claimed in this record
blocking_findings.impact: A relation load or CRUD operation held in Created beyond its configured command duration can still dispatch SQL in candidate7ad, whereas the fixed Rust adapter reaches Session::execute with zero remaining duration and returns NW_TIMEOUT/code8 before dispatch. This includes queue time after Start.
blocking_findings.minimal_correction: Capture the original per-entry admission instant and timeout at the matching Rust locations; saturating-subtract elapsed monotonic time in the two operation closures before Session::execute. Preserve cancellation-before-timeout priority, mutation bulk progress, and existing raw-SQL/Fluent timeout origin.
blocking_findings.necessary_regression: Use actual public C ABI operations with copied metadata and values: hold valid relation and mutation Created handles beyond the duration, then Start; require timeout8, deterministic gate retirement and independent SQL proof of no mutation. Include immediate-start success. Do not implement an alternate fake operation state machine.
blocking_findings.observation: The Rust B14 adapters capture a monotonic admission instant during creation, then subtract all elapsed creation/start/queue time immediately before Session::execute. Candidate7ad passes the full timeout into Session::execute, which starts a new deadline at worker execution. DbOperation admission_deadline is not a command-budget adjustment.

baseline_locations: native/database/relations/host.rs: nw_db_relation_load_create_v1, Host capacity preflight before relation.load and projection lookup
blocking_findings.basis: complete fixed Rust relation Host adapter compared to candidate7ad; actual public-ABI reproduction is delegated and not claimed here
blocking_findings.impact: Valid registered relation/model/projection inputs under a smaller source limit can change their public error category from ResourceLimit to binding invalid-argument. Combined over-limit plus wrong-projection cases also lose the original preflight priority.
blocking_findings.minimal_correction: Restore the four Host preflight conditions after borrowing the key and before projection lookup/compile_relation, using bounded or overflow-safe arity arithmetic. Retain the existing private compile_relation validation and its original binding error mapping.
blocking_findings.necessary_regression: Actual public C ABI rejections for finite key/arity/node/depth limits, zero output and no operation/SQL admission; include a wrong-projection combined case to retain priority. Validate exact supported boundary successes where representable.
blocking_findings.observation: The Rust Host rejects key bytes above the source binding byte limit, key arity above the parameter limit, arity*3 above the node limit, and depth below2 with Error::capacity (NW_DOMAIN_ERROR/code6). Candidate7ad omits this Host preflight and falls through to the private binding compiler, whose corresponding invalid condition maps to NW_INVALID_ARGUMENT/code11. Candidate projection lookup also precedes the missing Host preflight.

conclusion: The fully read query/mutation compiler files have no additional identified blocker, but adjacent public B14 Host adapters have two unresolved compatibility defects. Full candidate7ad technical approval is withheld pending correction and validation.
